messages.author: 1e1f02e079119aa4
messages.subject: Modeling prey behavioral responses
parts:
Hello,

I set up camera traps at 22 locations over the course of a winter and would like to assess whether prey (deer) temporarily avoid sites when predators (wolves) are in the vicinity or have been recently.  I can see two strategies to do this, and would love any feedback on whether one makes more sense than the other (or some third option that I haven't thought of).

Strategy 1:
Divide the winter into 50 primary sampling occasions, each with 3 secondary occasions (days), then use "number of wolves detected" (or else predicted wolf abundance) in each primary occasion at each site as a yearly sampling covariate in pcountOpen models for deer.  If I understand these models correctly, "wolf abundance" could affect either deer gamma or omega (or both) but not deer lambda (since it's time-invariant). 

Strategy 2:
Run a simple occu model where deer psi is constant (deer were detected at all sites at least once) but where "wolf presence" on a given day is used as a sampling covariate in the deer p function.  Then the interpretation would be along the lines of, "we know that deer occur in all sites, but when wolves are detected at a given site, deer are more/less/equally likely to be detected there".  Then I could also test for effects of time-lags in behavioral response as well.

In other words, both strategies would get at temporal rather than spatial predation avoidance.  I could see either of these working, but clearly if one was more robust, defensible, or appropriate than the other, I'd go with that.  Any feedback is very appreciated!

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Modeling prey behavioral responses
parts:
hi Jaya,
 It seems to me that you need to build a more complex hierarchical model in which both deer and wolf occupancy state are random variables and one depends on the other. there are papers by MacKenzie et al. 2004 (on species co-occurrence patterns) and a more recent one by Waddle et al. (http://www.esajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1890/09-0850.1)
which express the basic ideas very clearly. I suggest starting there and maybe what you need is a temporally dynamic version of such models which would be easy to do in WinBUGS.
regards
andy
